findings.title: Sealed Windows manifest is always rejected by required-member string comparison
findings.impact: The sole proposed real entry cannot reach independent-review or allocation validation even after those prerequisites exist: manifest.json uses code\entry.py and other backslash keys, whereas read_ready requires literal code/entry.py and five other forward-slash strings. Python string-set membership does not normalize Windows separators. The package therefore raises Complete preparation source set required unconditionally. This blocks Task 3 readiness and any PASS_PREPARATION_ONLY disposition.
evidence: Independently read the actual 172-key sealed manifest: none of the required slash-prefixed code/, harness/, inputs/ strings exists.
verification/prepare_review.py:70 serializes str(p.relative_to(N)), producing Windows backslashes.
tests/test_entry.py:19 creates hand-written forward-slash keys, so the saved 25 passing entry tests miss the real serializer/reader incompatibility.
findings.recommendation: Make the manifest producer and required-member reader use one canonical relative-path representation, while retaining traversal and hash checks. Add a regression using the actual preparation serializer/path representation and a read-only readiness check of the newly sealed package with synthetic review/allocation confined to a separate fixture. Preserve this failed manifest and review; do not relabel them PASS.
